title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Asha Raman
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes active decision records (ADRs) that affect these standards. The goal is to provide a single reference teams can use when designing or reviewing services that integrate with the Redwood inference platform.

Scope:
Applies to all backend services, inference runtimes, integration endpoints, and infrastructure owned by Engineering and Platform teams. Exceptions require an ADR and written approval from the relevant service owner and the Architecture Review Board.

Principles (short):
- Consistency: predictable APIs, error formats, and telemetry reduce integration overhead.
- Performance-first: meet latency and throughput targets by design; measure in real workloads.
- Observability-first: every service must emit metrics, structured logs, and traces.
- Safe rollouts: automated canaries, rollout policies, and rollback plans for any change touching production.
- Secure defaults: secrets, least privilege, and network segmentation by default.

1) API Standards

Summary:
APIs should be simple, versioned, well-documented, and secure. Standard patterns below describe acceptable request/response formats, authentication, pagination, error handling, and rate limiting.

Key rules:
- Naming and style: use RESTful resource paths (snake-case or kebab-case across the board), e.g. /v1/models/{model_id}/routes. Use nouns, not verbs.
- Versioning: include API major version in path (/v1/). Incompatible changes require a new major version and a published migration guide.
- Authentication: all endpoints require OAuth2 bearer tokens issued by Redwood IAM (or mTLS for private deployments). Tokens are validated at the edge.
- Rate limiting: default per-tenant rate limits configured in the API gateway; overflow must return 429 with Retry-After.
- Error responses: standard JSON envelope: {"error": {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional}}. Use HTTP status codes semantically.
- Pagination: cursor-based paging for list endpoints; include next_cursor and has_more.
- Streaming: use server-sent events (SSE) for token-streaming generation where supported; fallback to chunked responses.
- Contract checks: public API surface must include OpenAPI spec; CI validates contract against a canonical mock.

Example error (JSON):
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded for tenant",
    "details": {"limit": 120, "interval": "1m"}
  }
}

2) Coding Standards

Languages and tooling:
- Primary backend languages: Go (core runtime), Python (control plane, tooling), and TypeScript (web services). Use the idiomatic style guides for each language.
- Linters and formatters: gofmt/golangci-lint, pylint/ruff/black, eslint/prettier. CI enforces formatting and lint rules.
- Testing: unit tests for logic, integration tests for I/O boundaries, e2e smoke tests for critical flows (deployments, model rollout).
- PR requirements: at least one approving reviewer, passing CI (lint/test/security checks), and a documented changelog entry for public endpoints.

Code quality expectations:
- Maintainability: functions < 200 LOC, modules with clear responsibilities.
- Error handling: no swallowing errors; return and propagate contextualized errors.
- Dependency policy: follow platform-approved dependency lists; use Renovate for updates and require security review for new dependencies.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC and Runtime)

IaC and environments:
- Authoring: Terraform v1.5+ with Terragrunt where appropriate. Use module pattern in the company module registry.
- Environment parity: dev/staging/prod must use same Terraform modules and manifest schema. Differences limited to variable values.
- Secrets: AWS KMS-backed parameter store for hosted; customer-managed KMS for private deployments. Never commit secrets.
- Networking: VPC per environment, private subnets for runtimes, separate management plane subnets. ACLs and security groups must follow least privilege.

CI/CD:
- Pipeline: PR -> ci/lint/test -> canary deploy to staging -> automated smoke tests -> promote to prod. Production deploys to require two approvals for infra-affecting changes.
- Images: use SBOM-enabled container images; image provenance must be recorded in the registry.

Operational requirements:
- Ownership: services must declare an owner alias in service metadata. Oncall rotations must be defined in team runbooks.
- Capacity planning: SRE and service owners review capacity quarterly; autoscaling policies reviewed monthly.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Packaging and models:
- Model artifacts: store in versioned model registry with metadata (model_id, version, flavor, quantization_profile, digest).
- Supported formats: PyTorch, ONNX, and Firenze-optimized checkpoints. Containers must include deterministic loader and manifest.json.
- Quantization: apply curated quantization profiles from /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Document expected quality/regression impact.

Runtime behavior:
- Inference SLOs: per-model latency SLOs declared in model metadata (target_p50, p95, p99). The runtime enforces per-route timeouts and graceful degradation (fallback model variant).
- KV cache and prefix caching: services must implement configurable KV cache TTLs and prefix caching for repeated prompts. Cache invalidation rules must be documented for sensitive datasets.
- Batching: prefer dynamic batching with upper-bound latency budget. Batching policies should be declared with expected seq-length distribution.

Rollouts and compatibility:
- Rollouts: support canary (5-20%), A/B tests, and automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions.
- Model fallback: automatic fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., FP16 -> FP32) if resource constraints occur.
- Privacy: customer data must not be used for model retraining without explicit consent and a documented data handling ADR.

5) Observability Standards

Instrumentation:
- Metrics: emit Prometheus metrics with standard labels (tenant_id, model_id, route, zone). Include counters (requests_total), histograms (response_latency_seconds), and gauges (concurrency).
- Logs: structured JSON logs with trace_id, span_id, tenant_id, and severity. Use sampling on debug-level logs.
- Traces: OpenTelemetry traces with 200ms max parent span duration for generation loops and explicit spans for kernel selection, batching, and KV cache lookup.

Dashboards and alerts:
- Dashboards: per-service dashboards for traffic, errors, latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost, and cost-per-request.
- SLIs/SLOs: define at least request_success_rate and p95_latency. Default SLOs: request_success_rate >= 99.9% (monthly), p95_latency < 300ms for control-plane endpoints, and model-specific generation SLOs declared in metadata.
- Alerts: pager alert for SLO breach, infra degradation, and error-rate spikes. Alert thresholds documented in the team runbook.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarking

Targets and measurement:
- Latency budgets: control-plane RPCs <= 50ms p50, <= 200ms p95. Serving inference: model dependent; declare in metadata.
- Throughput: define expected throughput for each service and validate with load tests before production rollout.
- Benchmarking suite: teams must run canonical benchmark harness located in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Include representative prompt distributions and tokenization costs.

Benchmark report (table):
| Metric | Target | Measurement cadence | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| control_plane_p95_latency | < 200ms | daily | infra-team |
| inference_p95_latency (small-model) | < 150ms | daily | serving-runtime |
| inference_p95_latency (large-model) | < 800ms | daily | serving-runtime |
| request_success_rate | >= 99.9% monthly | monthly | service-owner |

7) ADRs (Summary of active decision records)

- ADR 2026-01: Runtime Kernel Selection (adopted) — deterministic kernel selection based on seq-length bucketing and device topology to reduce tail latency. Owner: runtime-team.
- ADR 2026-02: Quantization Baseline (adopted) — standardized set of quantization profiles with mandatory evals for quality regression checks. Owner: applied-ml.
- ADR 2026-03: API Versioning Policy (adopted) — major-version-in-path and semantic compatibility requirements for public APIs. Owner: eng-dx.
- ADR 2026-04: Default SLOs (adopted) — establish company-wide default SLOs for control plane and observability conventions. Owner: eng-sre.

For each ADR, include: intent, decision, consequences, and migration plan. See related ADR pages for full text.

8) Change and Review Process

- Architectural changes: require ADR. Minor standard changes (e.g., linter rules) can be approved by owners and documented in the repo CHANGELOG.
- Standards review cadence: quarterly architecture working group meeting to review proposed standard changes.

9) Ownership and Contacts

- Architecture owner: Platform Architecture (arch@redwood.ai)
- Runtime & Serving: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-team@redwood.ai)
- Observability & SRE: eng-sre (sre@redwood.ai)
- Applied ML & Evals: applied-ml-and-evals (ml-evals@redwood.ai)

10) Checklist for new services (must be completed before prod):
1. OpenAPI spec added and validated in CI.
2. Linting and unit tests pass in CI.
3. Integration/e2e smoke tests run in staging.
4. Dashboards created and onboarding alerts configured.
5. Owner alias and oncall rotation declared.
6. Capacity plan and autoscaling policy documented.
7. Model metadata (if applicable) published with SLOs and quantization profile.
8. ADR for any architectural deviations approved.

Appendix: Example rollout command (control-plane):
- Canary deploy (5%): ./deploy --service my-service --env prod --strategy canary --weight 5 --smoke-test ./ci/smoke.sh
- Rollback: ./deploy --service my-service --env prod --rollback latest_failed

References and links:
- Model quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Benchmark harness: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite
- ADR index: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-index

If you need to propose a change to these standards, open an ADR draft and link it to this page.
